about: Hyperlite's features, one row each, and the issue that tracks every gap. docs/roadmap.html shows it, with the live state of each issue (a closed issue shows as done). Update a row, and checked, in the PR that changes it: tests/test_roadmap.py refuses a release that cites a tracked issue the file was not reviewed for. status: ahead (extended), parity (available), partial, missing (planned).

rows.hl: hyperlite-cfs on Corosync, read-only without quorum, primary node for two-node clusters

Any node serves the dashboard and API v1, same accounts and sessions, and acts on any member's VMs, templates, networks, storage and ISO images (?node=, done by that member); a node that is down never holds a list or a call
Every node sends its VMs' summary every 10 s and at once after a change

rows.fr: Configuration répliquée, seule source de vérité
rows.en: Replicated configuration as the only source of truth
rows.hl: The cluster's configuration in hyperlite-cfs, applied by every node in one order, read-only without quorum; tasks, audit log, backups and their CSV exports of every node from any node; no controller (hosts driven over SSH: deprecated, gone with API v2)
The leader restarts a lost member's HA VMs once it is fenced, by priority and where they fit, with admission control and VM monitoring (restarted 80 s after its node was cut, in the lab)
Watchdog self-fencing of a node cut off, and a BMC power-off (IPMI, Redfish) confirmed before a restart; AMT power control still read-only

rows.fr: Verrous des disques sur le stockage partagé
rows.en: Disk locks on the shared storage
rows.hl: QEMU's image locks refuse a disk another node runs (checked on NFS 4.2, released 94 s after the node died); HA refused on a share whose locks stay on one node (NFS nolock or local_lock, SMB nobrl)
High, medium, low per VM, with preferred nodes
The loss of any one member must leave room for its HA VMs on the others: warn (default), strict or off
A guest that stops answering the QEMU guest agent, with no disk or network I/O, is reset in place by its node (at most three times an hour)

For the VMs on shared storage: off, manual or automatic, threshold 1 to 5, VMs together, apart, on or never on members (must or should, binding HA), per-VM exceptions, a drain that spreads the VMs, "Auto" placement of a new VM; moved in the lab 24 s after two VMs loaded their node
Drain by live migration, the VMs that stay listed with their reason
Rolling update: plan, maintenance, migration, update, reboot, one node after the other
Incremental replication to the other site every few minutes, guided recovery

rows.fr: Plusieurs clusters et sites depuis une seule vue
rows.en: Several clusters and sites from one view
rows.hl: Every cluster views the others (Sites page): their state, nodes and problems, a search through all their VMs, power actions and moves between a remote's nodes with a manage token; VMs moved between clusters offline or live (as qm remote-migrate --online, the target's libvirt behind a filtering relay), over pinned HTTPS, served by any node
Yes, shared pools created on every node

Per VM, tag or pool; GFS retention; weekly verification
Built in, no backup server

Every disk type (qcow2, raw, ZFS, LVM, iSCSI) into a backup store; a running VM's qcow2 disks read only where the guest wrote since the last backup (dirty bitmaps); every backup a complete image, never a chain

A chunk store as PBS's: 4 MiB chunks held once across every VM, optional client-side AES-256-GCM with a master recovery key, verification, garbage collection, off-site copies pulled by the other site (another store or another cluster, a read-only account, no key there) with their own retention

A backup restored as a new VM that starts at once, its disks copied while it runs (block pull): from a backup kept as files, or from a backup store (encrypted or not) served to QEMU by the node as a read-only NBD export

The API runs as www-data and reads libvirt through its read-only socket; hyperlite-daemon (root, local socket) does root's work after checking each call's proof and rights, opens the sessions and signs them with keys only root reads; the calls between nodes are signed with each node's own key

The same layout from 1.1 (/var/lib/hyperlite, /usr/lib/hyperlite); from 1.14 /etc/hyperlite is the replicated cluster configuration as read-only files (FUSE): priv/ root's, nodes/<host>/ with each node's certificate and keys, local pointing at this node's, .members, .version, .quorum
